If Mel Kiper's initial mock drafts over the last 5 years were 100% accurate, here's who your team would have drafted:

• It has nearly the same UI as reddit (which has always been rather poor)

  • It lifts concepts (subverse/subreddit, upvoat/upvote, etc.)

  • Certain subverses borrow their names from subreddits (/v/malefashionadvice immediately comes to mind)

I consider it a bad sign that the site takes almost all of its cues from reddit. Reddit had the benefit of being able to improve over time. One could argue that at while it's great that voat is picking up where reddit left off, it could just immediately re-enact the same problems.

I have no idea how to do this however. The formula works well.
I think we should do more to distinguish voat from reddit.

I'd like to see what some older (people that used Digg, then switched to Reddit) users could contribute in this question. IMO picking up where reddit left off is a good thing, if we manage to make this platform stay true to it's core values from where it was built. That's my two cents. :)
